evidence_summary: Fuzzboxes documents Universal Amplifier Corp. as the maker of the Astro Amp Astrotone, with the earliest known examples dating to 1967 and surviving potentiometer date codes proving production into 1969. Astro Amp literature gives a New York City address at 615 West 131st Street.

Fuzzboxes identifies the Sam Ash Fuzzz Boxx as the best-known rebrand supplied by Universal Amplifier Corp. and notes that black Astrotone and red Sam Ash versions were built during overlapping production. Sam Ash's historical page also states that the house-branded Fuzzz Boxx was manufactured by Universal Amplifier Corp. and introduced in 1968.

The builder's business location is documented at 615 West 131st Street in New York City in Astro Amp literature. Surviving production evidence and specialist reconstruction work support a distinct New York manufacturer rather than an inferred relationship to the nearby East Coast Fuzz family.

UMI is documented as a separate New York company founded by Richard Soloway around 1967. Its Buzz Tone is independently cataloged as a U.S.-produced late-1960s/early-1970s fuzz. The record is kept separate from Universal Amplifier Corp. despite geographic and component overlap among New York builders.

Specialist reconstruction divides early Astrotone production into multiple physical states, with an early version dated to late 1966/early 1967 and later green-PCB examples carrying 1969 date codes. Because surviving examples anchor the production window but do not provide a dated factory start document, the earlier 1966 claim remains below the high-confidence 1967 start.

Sam Ash's own historical account states the house-branded Fuzzz Boxx followed the Astrotone and was renamed in 1968. Fuzzboxes describes the red Fuzzz Boxx as the mass-produced Sam Ash-marketed version and records later production into the late 1960s or early 1970s, but the exact cutoff remains unresolved.

Universal Amplifier Corp. appears to have been a distinct small New York manufacturer responsible for Astro Amp products. Its later corporate fate is unknown in the current source set, so the company should not be conflated with UMI, Applied Audio, or other New York/New Jersey manufacturers merely because their products share period components.
